scope: Only whether the exact two .pyi annotations are Python grammar errors; no claim they are valid portable type annotations or that the stub body is fully supported.

typing_stub_spec.interpretation: Stub files must be syntactically valid Python and parseable using ast.parse. Static annotation interpretation is as quoted, and portable supported constructs form a subset; type checkers may ignore unsupported constructs. This does not turn every unsupported type expression into a Python grammar error.

annotation_spec.interpretation: Type/annotation expressions are a restricted subset for the type system, whereas the Python language permits arbitrary expressions in annotations. A named expression need not be a valid type expression; Python grammar acceptance and type-checker support are distinct.

intended_contract: The .pyi suffix does not itself activate the compiler future-annotations mode. Each exact original has no absolute future directive, and actual CPython3.10.19 ast.parse and compile accept it. The certificate removes only the pinned generic invalid-syntax false positive, not any dedicated type-system diagnostic. Expected[] asserts no selected PYI019/PYI034 finding or Python grammar error; it does not certify the source as a valid portable typed stub.
independence: Compiler observations come from the preserved actual39-source CPython run; unrelated invalid/relative-future bug examples are not evidence for these two cases. Existing full fixture positives remain unchanged.
